ysolde_first.title: COFFEE WITH YARA
ysolde_first.text: 'News is the one thing that grows in value,' says Yara, stirring a coffee she will not drink. 'For one big favour I will tell you who in this building is lying to you. For free, I will tell you to be careful.'

left.label: Say no
left.result: 'Careful, then,' says Yara, and slides you a coffee you did not ask for.

right.label: Do her the favour
right.memo: You bought a secret from Yara.
branches: She slides over a folded note. The head of the CEO's office sells the CEO's daily plans. To her, and to others.
'Quentin? He never sells. I have tried.' It is the nearest thing to praise she gives anyone.

lesson.left: Saying no keeps your hands clean and your favours free. But you stay the one who does not know what everyone else knows.
lesson.right: Bought news is only as good as the seller's reasons. A broker will sell the same true thing to you and to others.

ysolde_ledger.title: THE LONG THREAD
ysolde_ledger.text: 'I keep screenshots,' says Yara. 'Your name has a long thread now. Favours, pressure, a few neat lies. Others would pay well to read it. I would much rather be your friend.'

left.label: Buy the screenshots
left.memo: You bought the screenshots that had your name.
left.result: The files change hands. Yara keeps a copy, as you would have done.

right.label: Call her bluff
right.memo: You called Yara's bluff about the screenshots.
right.result: She shrugs, and for once she looks unsure. Maybe she was bluffing.
branches: Yara sells the thread to the highest buyer by morning. Every message leads back to you.
A few screenshots turn up in the leadership chat. It is not the worst page. It is bad enough.

lesson.left: Paying to keep a record hidden costs less than defending your name. It also keeps the broker in your story.
lesson.right: Daring a record keeper to publish bets that she values her trade more than the sale. Sometimes she does not.

king_ill.title: THE NUMBERS ARE OFF
king_ill.text: Lucas shuts the door and does not sit. 'The quarterly numbers. I have audited many reports. This one is wrong. Someone is changing the figures a little each week.'

left.label: Look into it quietly
left.memo: You looked into the numbers in secret.
left.result: Lucas gives you a spreadsheet and a list of odd entries. You tell no one.

right.label: Tell the leadership team
right.memo: You told the leadership team about the numbers.
right.result: The room erupts. Everyone looks shocked. Some of them are very good actors.

lesson.left: Staying silent keeps the guilty one comfortable, and comfortable people repeat their habits. You bought time with your own safety.
lesson.right: Telling everyone warns the one who changed the numbers as well as the victim. It also makes you the person who raised the alarm.

tasting_cup.title: THE REPORT TO SIGN
tasting_cup.text: Before the board meeting, the CEO hands you the quarterly report. It is a kind gesture and a sign of trust. Lucas's eyes find yours across the room. The numbers look perfect. A little too perfect.

left.label: Ask an analyst to check it first
left.memo: You had an analyst check the CEO's report.
left.result: The analyst finds errors within the hour. The report was bad. The office is shocked, quietly.

right.label: Sign it yourself
branches: Lucas's notes keep you safe. The board watches someone sign a clean report with proof behind it.
You sign. Later, the report is found false. The last thing you see is Lucas walking away, and nobody else.
You are called in, grey in the face. The report was bad. You clear your name in a week. The office tells the story for much longer.

lesson.left: A second check keeps your own hands clean, but someone else does the work, and they did not choose it. People notice who was told to be careful.
lesson.right: Signing yourself shows strong belief. It can also end your career if you do not know what you are signing.

poisoner_unmasked.title: WHO CHANGED THE FIGURES
text: Lucas has traced the changes to the finance team Oliver Vasquez set up. 'He has a reason. A weak quarter gives him more control. He has the means too. That is not proof. But I would check his invoices.'
Lucas has traced the changes to Selena's sales team. 'Her top manager entered the numbers, and he is terrified. Selena is calm. Either she is innocent, or she is a great actress.'
Lucas has traced the changes to the CEO's office. 'Quentin's login made the edits that night. Was it for money or from fear? I cannot say. But it was his login.'

left.label: Remove the guilty one quietly
left.memo: You had the person behind the numbers removed quietly.
left.result: It happens in a quiet meeting on Friday. By Monday, the guilty one has simply left the company.

right.label: Show the proof to the board
right.memo: You showed the board who changed the numbers.
right.result: The board watches {culprit} being walked out. For one afternoon, everyone is on the same side.

lesson.left: A quiet exit ends the danger but leaves questions. Rumours grow from questions.
lesson.right: A public hearing gives you the most right to act. It also teaches the next cheat what to hide.

anonymous_note.title: A MESSAGE FROM "I.V."
anonymous_note.text: A private message pops up from an account with no photo. 'Your rise was no accident. Your fall does not have to be one either. Name a place and a time.' It is written by someone who never asks permission.

left.label: Ignore the message
left.result: You delete it. The next day, a faint perfume lingers in the lift, which is somehow worse.

right.label: Name a place and a time
right.result: A courier delivers the reply to a car outside the building and vanishes before you finish reading.

lesson.left: Letting a mystery person come to you keeps the first move. But you are now ignoring a powerful person.
lesson.right: Choosing the time and place of a secret meeting feels like control. It only helps if you know who you are meeting.

veiled_meeting.title: THE CAR WITH DARK WINDOWS
text: The car is waiting outside your building this time. 'It was rude not to answer,' says a calm voice. 'I forgive it once. I can make the board lean your way. All I will ask is a name, when the time comes.'

A car with dark windows waits outside the parking garage. The woman inside never takes off her sunglasses. 'I can make the board lean your way,' she says. 'All I will ever ask is a name, when the time comes.'

left.label: Refuse the helper
left.result: The window stays shut. The car drives off at exactly the speed limit.

right.label: Accept her help
right.memo: You accepted the Silent Sponsor's help.
right.result: By the next board meeting, three locked doors are open.

lesson.left: Refusing an unknown helper keeps you free. It also makes you a fixed point that someone must now work around.
lesson.right: A helper makes you depend on her, and she depends on you. But only she knows how long the leash is.

veiled_price.title: THE NAME
veiled_price.text: The same quiet voice again. 'The name I mentioned,' it says. 'My nephew, a young vice president. When the CEO steps down, you will back him and no one else. I have waited a long time to ask.'

left.label: Refuse
left.memo: You refused the Silent Sponsor's price.
left.result: Doors close in the order they opened. Her favour was a staircase, and she has taken it away.

right.label: Promise to back her nephew
right.memo: You promised to back the Silent Sponsor's pick.
right.result: You agree in the car park. It is the first thing you cannot take back.

lesson.left: Refusing the price loses what you already gained. It also shows others you can say no to the most powerful person in the room.
lesson.right: The price of free help is shown last. Paying keeps you safe. It also ties your future choices to someone else's plan.

unveiling.title: THE PARKING PASS
unveiling.text: The same dark car passes your window again. The driver stops to fix a mirror. For one breath, the parking pass on the dash is visible, with a name on it. You could follow it.

left.label: Let it go
left.result: The car turns the corner. Some mysteries are more useful when left alone.

right.label: Follow the car
right.memo: You followed the Silent Sponsor's car.
right.result: It ends at the private entrance of Isabel Venn, Chair of the Board.
branches: It ends at the Chair's private door. Her driver looks straight at you. You have been seen.

lesson.left: Leaving a secret alone keeps you off a powerful person's list. It also keeps you blind to the hand that moves the pieces.
lesson.right: Finding out who a helper is gives you power and a weakness. She will wonder what else you have learned.

sabel_gift.title: A GIFT WITH NO STRINGS
sabel_gift.text: Imre from Southline Group hands you a premium tablet and a free pilot of his software. 'A gift from Southline. No strings, only friendship.' The box is beautifully made, like most traps.

left.label: Refuse the gift
left.result: Imre nods. Only a very good salesperson is so kind about a refusal.

right.label: Accept it
right.result: It is a lovely thing. You find yourself thinking of it whenever Imre is in the room.

lesson.left: Refusing a gift keeps things clean. It costs a little warmth with someone who offered it to build some.
lesson.right: A gift with "no strings" costs less than most and more than it seems. You owe the favour even if the bill never comes.

sabel_treaty.title: A CONTRACT BY MORNING
text: 'Sign the partnership contract by morning,' says Imre, resting a hand on the tablet he gave you. 'Southline is generous but in a hurry.' In the corner, Oliver shakes his head slightly. Oliver has his own reasons to dislike a rival.
'Sign the partnership contract by morning,' says Imre. 'Southline is generous but in a hurry.' In the corner, Oliver shakes his head slightly. Oliver has his own reasons to dislike a rival.

left.label: Sign it now
branches: Money flows in. Somewhere in the small print is a clause that nobody read out loud.
The contract is exactly what it said it was. Imre looks truly relieved.

right.label: Wait and check it
right.memo: You waited to check the contract.
branches: Page nine gives Southline admin access to our core systems. Imre's charm gets thinner.
The contract is fair. Imre is hurt that you doubted him, and not completely wrong to be.

lesson.left: Signing fast rewards the one who set the deadline. Whether it was a mistake depends on what was in the contract.
lesson.right: Asking for time to read what you sign is a normal right. People in a hurry treat it as an insult. Being rushed is a warning sign.

sabel_betrayal.title: A BACK DOOR, NOT A PARTNERSHIP
sabel_betrayal.text: Southline "support engineers" are inside our systems, and there are a great many of them. Dana storms in with a printout. 'You gave them the keys. They never needed a partnership. They needed a back door.'

left.label: Cancel the contract in public
left.note: Imre tricked you with the contract.
left.memo: You cancelled Southline's contract in public.
left.result: You admit the mistake in front of the company and cut Southline off. Dana runs to lock down the systems.

right.label: Say it was all planned
right.note: Imre tricked you with the contract.
right.memo: You said the contract was part of a plan.
right.result: You tell leadership it is a trap for Southline. Nobody believes it, and a few pretend to.

lesson.left: Owning a mistake early limits the damage. It makes your next words easier to believe.
lesson.right: A bluff that hides your own mistake works until someone checks. Then you have two problems.
